method.summary:
Global reservoir watch: the Kariba 'next' method applied to every major hydro reservoir in G-REALM.

    python3 -m pipeline.reservoirs        -> web/public/data/reservoirs.json

Method (fixed before any crisis was scored; see docs/RESERVOIRS.md):
  1. Monthly satellite lake level (NASA/USDA G-REALM 10-day altimetry).
  2. Target: the level against its own same-calendar-month history from earlier years only.
     warning = below the 20th percentile, danger = below the 10th percentile.
  3. ENSO sensitivity: wet-season level change (lake's own low month -> high month) in El Nino vs
     other seasons and La Nina vs other seasons (mean ONI over the wet-season months), two-sided
     permutation tests.
  4. Forecast: analog ensemble of historical 12-month level changes added to the current level
     (capped at the highest level seen). Analogs are phase-conditioned (by the ONI known at issue)
     only when step 3, computed from past seasons only, gives p < 0.1 for that phase; otherwise
     all past years (climatology analogs).
  5. Strictly forward backtest, issued monthly, horizons 1-12; scores from Jan 2000.
method.target: warning = monthly level below the 20th percentile of the same calendar month in earlier years; danger = below the 10th percentile. Percentiles use the lake's own satellite record, so the altimetry datum (EGM2008) cancels and no storage curve is needed.
method.forecast: Analog ensemble: current level + each past year's 12-month level change from the same calendar month, capped at the highest level seen. Phase-conditioned analogs (El Nino / La Nina / neutral seasons, by the ONI season ending the month before issue) only when the lake's wet-season ENSO test, recomputed each January from past seasons only, has p < 0.1 for that phase and at least 8 seasons; otherwise all past years. At least 3 analogs per phase pool, else all years.
method.issue_convention: Issue month t uses levels through month t-1 and the ONI season ending in t-1. Horizon h targets month t+h-1.
method.baselines: Climatology = share of earlier same-month levels below the threshold (about 0.2). Persistence = 1 if the latest month is below its own warning threshold, else 0.
method.alarm_rule: Alarm at an issue = P(below warning) > 0.5 in any of the next 12 months (Kariba's rule).
method.episode_rule: Observed warning episode onset = first month below warning after at least 3 months not below. Hit = an alarm issued 1-12 months before onset. False-alarm run = consecutive alarm issues starting while the lake is not below warning, with no month below warning from the run start to 11 months after its end.
method.backtest: Strictly forward, issued monthly 1998-01..2026-11, scored on issues from 2000-01 and observed targets only. Wet season, ENSO gate, thresholds and analogs all come from data before each issue.
method.crisis_rule: Crisis caught = first alarm in the 12 issues up to the onset month was issued before the onset month; lead = onset month - alarm month. Rule fixed before scoring; not tuned per crisis.

summary.headline: 31 hydro reservoirs (77 GW at the dams, 22 GW more downstream) watched from space. In a strictly forward backtest the method caught 14 of 17 documented crises ahead of onset (median lead 12 months) and beats climatology at 1-10 months.
summary.headline_risk: Highest live risk of falling below the warning level in the next 12 months: Cahora Bassa 100%, Kainji 100%, La Vueltosa (Uribante-Caparo) 100%, Srisailam 100%, Toktogul 69%.

record.datum: m above EGM2008 geoid (satellite altimetry, not the operator's gauge datum; percentiles make the datum irrelevant)

history_percentile_track.note: p10/p20 for the current month use earlier years only; by_month uses the whole record (display only)

limitations: Satellite altimetry level is not the operator's gauge level (different datum and point of measurement). Percentiles of the lake's own record avoid the datum problem, but a percentile is not a usable-storage fraction: a low percentile may still be well above minimum operating level, and vice versa.
Percentile thresholds depend on the record length (5 to 33 years). Early in the record, and for lakes starting in 2008, the 10th and 20th percentiles rest on few years.
Operations (release decisions, new upstream dams, rule curves) change level behaviour. Analogs assume past level changes are representative.

Analogs add the past 12-month level change to today's level, capped at the highest level seen. This ignores the lake's shape (a metre is more water when the lake is full) and minimum-level operating limits.
The ENSO outlook in backtests is the ONI known at issue (persistence), not an archived ENSO forecast; issues before an event develops (boreal spring) see the wrong phase.
Several lakes have multi-year gaps (2002-2008 for lakes off the TOPEX/Jason track); no forecasts are made across gaps.
Crisis dates come from news and official statements; several give only the month. Multi-reservoir crises are scored on one pre-chosen main reservoir.
Lake Victoria and Lake Malawi levels drive run-of-river plants; Itaipu and Three Gorges levels are rule-driven and say little about drought.
